I read all 73 lines of the file. It has five theorems: anchor_power_lower, anchor_halved_power_lower, anchor_branch_lower, anchored_interval_budget and anchored_density_budget. Each one is a hypothesis-dependent `≤` estimate between explicit real expressions, such as `Real.exp (-((p + 2) ^ 3)) ≤ delta ^ (2 * m) / 40`. The file has no definitions, structures, equations or iff statements, and no simp, norm_cast or other rewriting attributes. None of the proofs uses `simp`. The only rewrites are steps with existing Mathlib lemmas (`Real.exp_sub`, `Real.exp_add`, `Real.exp_nat_mul`) inside individual proofs.

I searched the project for uses of these theorems. Inside the file, the helper lemmas are passed as explicit proof terms. Outside it, the only uses are in lean/OAI/Combinatorics/Progressions/Lattices/AnchoredIntegerIntervalsPower.lean (lines 97 and 105–106), where `anchored_density_budget` and `anchored_interval_budget` are also used as explicit terms, for example `(anchored_interval_budget hp hm hdelta).trans hbias`.

These lemmas would not work well as simp lemmas. Each needs side hypotheses such as `hdelta : Real.exp (-p) ≤ delta`, and they give quantitative bounds rather than canonical forms. Nothing in the file introduces a new expression that would need a simp normal form. So there is no simp lemma, attribute, rewrite direction or possible cycle for this rubric to judge, and I report no findings.
